items.title: Carrosserie Kris
items.abstract: Local body shop website iterated on continuously since 2021 - performance, SEO, and conversion improvements shipped across a four-year client relationship.

business.summary: A long-term retainer relationship, not a one-off build. The site is the shop's primary lead channel: fast, findable on Google, and with contact forms that reliably convert visits into quote requests.
outcomes: Steady inbound quote requests through the website
Client trusts one partner for updates and maintenance

engineering.summary: React frontend with a Node.js backend, styled with Tailwind. The codebase is optimized for Core Web Vitals and kept evergreen through regular dependency and content updates.
decisions: Mobile-first layout system; animations kept off the critical path
Image and asset pipeline tuned for Largest Contentful Paint
Form handling hardened against spam without hurting conversion
Small, boring stack chosen deliberately for long-term maintainability

items.title: Banden Leusch
items.abstract: New website for a full-service garage and tyre centre in Grobbendonk: maintenance, wheel alignment and ADAS calibration, tyres and key service on one fast page. I host and maintain the site.

business.summary: A new website to replace the old one: every service the garage offers, from tyres and rims to ADAS calibration and key service, laid out clearly on one page, with a contact form that sends the car's details straight away. I have hosted and maintained the site since it launched in 2026.
outcomes: Every service on one clear page
Contact form with make, model, year and VIN
Hosted and maintained by the developer

engineering.summary: Next.js, statically prerendered, with Tailwind for styling and cookieless analytics through a self-hosted Umami. One page, with an anchor per service in the navigation.
decisions: Statically prerendered: the page is served ready-made from the cache
Cookieless analytics through a self-hosted Umami
Vehicle details as separate form fields, so an enquiry is usable straight away

items.title: Distributed Intrusion Detection and Prevention System
items.abstract: Distributed intrusion detection and prevention for educational networks. An inline edge device captures traffic, a remote server analyzes it, and block rules are enforced locally without slowing the network.

business.summary: Schools get enterprise-grade network protection on commodity hardware. Threats are detected and blocked in real time, while staff see everything on a single live dashboard - no security team required on site.
outcomes: Real-time threat detection and automatic blocking
One dashboard for the whole network - no specialist needed
Runs on a Raspberry Pi: minimal hardware investment

engineering.summary: A Rust capture agent runs inline on a Raspberry Pi, streams packet data to a VPS for Suricata-based analysis, and applies verdicts locally so the hot path never blocks on the network round-trip.
decisions: Rust on the edge: memory-safe packet handling, zero GC pauses inline
Capture and enforcement decoupled from analysis - fail-open by design
Server-side pipeline containerized with Docker for reproducible deploys
Suricata rule engine drives detection; custom layer handles prevention

items.title: Provilion Broodjes
items.abstract: Full-stack lunch ordering platform for a school, fully built but never put into use: students order, parents manage credits, administrators run daily operations, with integrated payment processing.

business.summary: A self-service ordering system meant to replace the cash and Excel behind a school's sandwich sales: ordering and paying in the Wednesday break, collecting on Friday. Parents top up credits online, Stripe settles the orders and the kitchen works from one live dashboard. The platform was fully built, but never put into use.
outcomes: Ordering and paying fully online, with no cash changing hands at break time
Parents control spending through a prepaid credit system
Admin dashboard turns daily orders into a single prep list

engineering.summary: Next.js and TypeScript end to end, MySQL for persistence, and Stripe webhooks driving payment reconciliation. Role-based access control separates student, parent, and administrator capabilities.
decisions: Webhook-driven payment flow: credit balances only mutate on confirmed events
RBAC enforced at the API layer, not just hidden in the UI
Transactional order writes keep credit ledger and orders consistent
Email notifications decoupled from the request path

items.title: Het Smaakpand (Closed)
items.abstract: Clean, minimal website for a local sandwich shop: menu display, opening hours, mobile-first. Retired when the business closed its doors.

business.summary: A small business got online fast and affordably. The site did one job - show the menu and get people through the door - and did it without ongoing complexity or cost.
highlights: No maintenance incidents while the site ran
outcomes: Menu and hours instantly findable from any phone
No CMS overhead for a shop with a stable menu
Cleanly decommissioned when the business closed

engineering.summary: Static-first delivery with a deliberately minimal footprint. No frameworks where none were needed - fast loads, trivial hosting, and nothing to patch.
decisions: Static delivery: no server runtime, near-zero attack surface
Hand-tuned CSS instead of a framework for a single-page footprint
Sub-second loads on mobile networks as the primary target
Archived with a clean teardown - no orphaned infrastructure

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.metaDescription: What data brentweb.be processes, why and for how long: cookieless analytics, forms, phone and WhatsApp, and the map that only loads after a click.

sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: This Privacy Policy explains how Brent Schoenmakers ("I", "me" or "my") collects, uses and protects your personal data when you visit this website (brentweb.be). I am the controller of this data and can be reached at brent@brentweb.eu.

sections.title: Analytics Data
paragraphs: I use Umami, a cookieless analytics tool that I host myself on my own server in Germany (Hetzner, Nuremberg). It stores nothing in your browser: no cookies, no local storage, no visitor ID. Your IP address is used only to derive an approximate country and a daily-rotating, non-reversible hash, and is never stored. I see only aggregated figures:

list.text: Pages visited and how long visits last
Browser, operating system and device type
Referral source (how you found this website)
Approximate country

afterList: No data is shared with or sold to third parties, and it is never shown on the public website. If your browser sends a Do Not Track signal, nothing is recorded.

sections.title: Forms, Cost Estimator & Website Check
paragraphs: When you use the contact form, the cost estimator or the free website check, I collect:

list.text: Your name and email address

Your message and the project details you provide: budget, timeline and optionally your business website on the contact form, or your answers, an optional project description, company name and notes in the cost estimator
For the free website check: your website address, to prepare the report and send it to you

afterList: I use this information solely to respond to your inquiry. It is sent via Resend (an email delivery service) to my inbox and to yours as a confirmation, and stored in my customer relationship system (CRM), which I host myself. It is not shared with any other party. Submissions are rate-limited by IP address to prevent abuse; that counter is held only in server memory, is never written to disk, and is discarded automatically after a short period of inactivity. A hidden field on every form helps detect spam and contains no personal data.

sections.title: Phone and WhatsApp
paragraphs: If you call me or send a WhatsApp message, I see your phone number, and with WhatsApp also your profile name and what you write. I only use that to answer your question and keep it no longer than needed, at most 12 months, unless it leads to a project.

The phone and WhatsApp buttons on this site are plain links: nothing is loaded from WhatsApp or Meta until you click one yourself. The self-hosted analytics only counts that such a link was clicked, without your number.

sections.title: Legal Bases
paragraphs: I only process your data where the GDPR provides a basis for it:

list.label: Consent (Art. 6(1)(a)):
list.text: for analytics, and for processing what you send through a form

list.label: Pre-contractual steps (Art. 6(1)(b)):
list.text: to answer your inquiry and prepare a quote

list.label: Legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)):
list.text: for site security, such as rate limiting and spam detection, and for the functional preference cookies
Form messages and inquiries: up to 12 months, unless they lead to a project and statutory accounting retention applies
Analytics data: up to 14 months
Preference cookies (bw-locale and bw-path): one year

sections.title: Cookies and Local Storage
paragraphs: This website uses:

list.label: Essential storage:
list.text: required for the site to work, such as remembering your theme preference

list.label: Preference cookies:
list.text: two first-party cookies remember how you browse. bw-locale stores your chosen language and bw-path stores whether you entered through the business or the engineering section, so returning visits land on the right page. Neither contains personal data and neither is shared.

afterList: You can also control cookies through your browser settings. Disabling them may affect how parts of the site work.

sections.title: Data Security
paragraphs: Measures I take to protect your information include:

list.text: HTTPS encryption for all traffic
Strict Transport Security (HSTS)
Rate limiting on every form, to reduce abuse
Regular security updates and monitoring

afterList: No transmission over the internet is completely secure, so I cannot guarantee absolute security.

sections.title: Third-Party Services
paragraphs: This website uses the following third-party services:

list.label: Resend:
list.text: delivers contact form and cost estimator emails, including the PDF estimate summary you request

list.label: Anthropic (Claude):
list.text: only if you click 'Analyse my description' in the cost estimator: your project description and answers are sent to Anthropic's API to analyse them. Your name and email address are not. Anthropic may process this data in the United States.

list.label: WhatsApp (Meta):
list.text: only if you contact me through WhatsApp yourself. WhatsApp's own privacy policy also applies to those messages.

list.label: Google Maps and OpenStreetMap:
list.text: the map at the bottom of the contact section only loads after you click "Show map" yourself. Before that click the site makes no connection to Google or OpenStreetMap at all. After it, that service receives your IP address among other things, as with any website visit, and its own privacy policy applies.

have inaccurate data corrected
have your data erased
restrict processing
object to processing based on legitimate interest
receive your data in a common format (portability)
withdraw consent at any time, without affecting processing that took place before

afterList: To exercise these rights, email brent@brentweb.eu. I will respond within one month.
If you are unhappy with how I handle your data, you can lodge a complaint with the Belgian Data Protection Authority, Rue de la Presse 35, 1000 Brussels (www.dataprotectionauthority.be).

1.q: What if I don't know what I need?
1.a: That's how most projects start, so it's not a problem. Tell me what's slowing you down in normal language and I'll tell you what it would take. Sometimes the honest answer is that you don't need me, and I'll say that too.

2.q: What if the project grows along the way?
2.a: Then you hear what the extra costs before I build it. I quote per project, not per hour, so you never get a surprise bill for extra hours.

3.q: Do I own what you build?
3.a: Yes. The code and the domain are yours: the domain is registered in your name, and I manage it along with the hosting and DNS. If you ever move to another developer or host, you get the code, your data and your domain's transfer code, at no extra cost and with nothing to buy back.

4.q: What if something breaks after launch?
4.a: If something I built breaks, I fix it. That's not a new project and I don't bill it as one.

5.q: Why is this cheaper than an agency?
5.a: There's no sales team, no project manager and no office to pay for. You're paying for the work itself instead of the overhead around it.

website.title: A website that actually brings in customers
website.intro: Fast, hand-built websites for freelancers and small businesses, findable on Google. You deal directly with the developer and know the price before I start.
forWho: You don't have a website yet, or have one you no longer dare to touch.
Your site is online, but it doesn't bring in calls or enquiries.
You don't want a website-builder subscription, but a site you own.
approach: We start with a conversation about what the site needs to achieve: calls, quote requests or visitors to your shop. Every page is built around that.
No template or page builder, so the site loads fast, even on a slow connection. I arrange the domain, hosting and SSL for you; the domain is registered in your name.

faq.q: How much does a website cost?
faq.a: Most websites cost between {websiteMin} and {websiteMax}, depending on the number of pages and what the site needs to do. You get a fixed price in writing before I start, and it doesn't change once we agree. As a small business I'm VAT-exempt, so nothing is added.

Usually {websiteWeeksMin} to {websiteWeeksMax} weeks, depending on the number of pages and whether the text is ready. You see something working every week, so we adjust before the site is finished rather than after.

faq.q: Can I update the website myself?
faq.a: Text and photos that change often can be set up so you edit them yourself. For anything else you email me, and I reply within a day or two.

A hand-built site that works well on a phone and is fast enough for Google, with hosting, the domain and SSL taken care of. Extras such as a contact form, a blog, a photo gallery, online booking or a web shop are your choice; the cost estimate shows what each one costs.

faq.q: I already have a website. Can you rebuild it?
faq.a: Yes. I move the content of your old site to the new one and redirect the old addresses to the new pages, so visitors and Google keep finding them.

faq.q: Can my website be in more than one language?
faq.a: Yes. A second language, such as French, Dutch or German, can be added. You supply the translations; I build the language versions and make sure Google shows each one separately.

faq.q: Will my website be found on Google?
faq.a: The basics are standard: fast pages, one clear page per service, correct titles and descriptions, and structured data so Google knows who you are and where. Nobody can promise the top spot, but a site built on that gives you the best chance.

needs: Your text and photos, or a rough version of them. If you don't have them, I can edit or write the text; that is then listed separately in the quote.
What you sell or do, and for whom. I build the pages around that, one per service.
If you already have a site or a domain, access to it. I move the content over and make sure your domain comes along.
Someone who responds within a few days to what I show you each week.

webApp.metaDescription: Replace shared spreadsheets and double data entry with one custom web application. From {webAppMin} to {webAppMax}, at a fixed price agreed up front.
webApp.title: A custom web application instead of another spreadsheet
webApp.intro: Does your business run on shared spreadsheets and retyped orders? I build one web application everyone logs into, where what's entered is right.
forWho: Several people work in the same Excel file and overwrite each other's work.
Orders or requests get typed in twice, in two different systems.
An off-the-shelf package does most of what you need, but not the part that matters most.
approach: First I map how the work runs today: who enters what, and where it goes wrong. The database is built around that.
You get accounts with per-role permissions, an admin area and checks that stop duplicate or wrong entries.

faq.q: How much does a custom web application cost?
faq.a: Usually between {webAppMin} and {webAppMax}, depending on the number of user roles, screens and integrations. You get a fixed price up front. If the scope grows along the way, you hear what it costs before I build it.
Yes. The code and the domain are yours; I manage the hosting and DNS. If you ever want to continue with another developer, you take everything with you and nothing is locked in.

faq.q: Can it connect to the tools I already use?
faq.a: Usually, yes. Most accounting packages, web shops, CRMs and payment providers have an API I can use to exchange data automatically.

faq.q: How long does a custom web application take?
faq.a: Usually {webAppWeeksMin} to {webAppWeeksMax} weeks. You get something working to test every week, so a wrong approach shows up early rather than at handover.

If an off-the-shelf package does what you need, it is almost always cheaper, and I'll say so. Custom software only pays off when the most important part of your work doesn't fit in one, or when you pay for ten features to use one.

faq.q: What if something goes wrong after handover?
faq.a: If something I built breaks, I fix it, and I don't bill it as a new project. A new feature is new work, with its own price up front.

needs: A walk through how the work runs today, with the spreadsheets, forms or emails you use now.
Who needs which rights: who enters data, who only reads, who manages.
Sample data, so I build and test against real cases instead of made-up ones.
One person on your side who decides when a choice has to be made.

integrations.metaDescription: Get your web shop, accounting, CRM and payments talking to each other, and automate repetitive work. From {integrationsMin}, fixed price up front.
integrations.title: Make your systems work together, without retyping
integrations.intro: A lot of manual work sits between two systems, like an order that has to go from the web shop to the accounts. I build the integration that does it automatically.
forWho: You copy data from one program into another by hand.
You do the same steps in the same order every day or week.
A payment provider, CRM or other package needs to exchange data with your website.
approach: I connect through the APIs of the services you already use, and test against the real service, not a mock.
If a step fails, the system retries and you get an alert. Scheduled jobs, such as a daily summary, run on their own.

faq.q: How much does an integration or automation cost?
faq.a: An integration with an external service usually costs {apiMin} to {apiMax}, automating a fixed process {automationMin} to {automationMax}. You get a fixed price up front.

faq.q: What if the other service changes something?
faq.a: The error handling catches it straight away, and you get an alert instead of wrong data. I adapt the integration, and you hear what that costs up front.

Anything with an API, which is most of them: accounting packages such as Exact Online, Yuki or Billit, CRMs such as Teamleader or HubSpot, web shops such as Shopify or WooCommerce, and payment providers such as Mollie or Stripe. If your package has no API, I'll tell you honestly whether there's another way.

faq.q: How long does an integration take?
faq.a: An integration with an external service usually takes {apiWeeksMin} to {apiWeeksMax} weeks, an automation {automationWeeksMin} to {automationWeeksMax} weeks. Most of the work is testing against the real service.
The integration only gets access to what it needs, and passwords or API keys are never in the code. If something goes wrong, it's logged and you get an alert.

Sometimes. A language model can help with reading or summarising text, such as incoming email. For fixed steps with fixed rules, an ordinary automation is more reliable and cheaper, and that's what I'd recommend.

needs: Access to the services that need connecting, ideally a separate account with only the rights the integration needs.
The steps you now do by hand, in the order you do them.
Who should get an alert when something goes wrong.

geelKempen.metaTitle: Website development in Geel and the Kempen
geelKempen.metaDescription: Web developer based in Geel. A fast, hand-built website for your business in the Kempen, straight from the developer and at a fixed price agreed up front.
geelKempen.eyebrow: WEB DESIGNER IN GEEL · THE KEMPEN
geelKempen.title: Having a website built in Geel and the Kempen
intro: I'm Brent, a web developer based in Geel. If you run a business in the Kempen, I build you a website that's written by hand, loads quickly on a phone, and gets found by people nearby who are looking for what you do.

You don't deal with an agency or a salesperson, but directly with the person building your site. We start with a free half-hour call. After that you get a fixed price in writing: no hourly billing and no surprises afterwards.

Getting found locally starts with the basics: a clear page for each service, an address and opening hours that are correct, and a site fast enough for Google. I pay attention to that from the very first page.
geelKempen.navLabel: Websites in Geel and the Kempen

sections.title: A web designer for the whole Kempen, not just Geel
paragraphs: I work from Geel for businesses across the Kempen: Mol, Herentals, Westerlo, Kasterlee, Olen, Turnhout, Grobbendonk and the villages in between. People in the region looking for a tradesperson, a shop or a service mostly search on a phone, and often add the name of their town.
That is why every service you offer gets a page of its own, with the towns you work in on it. That way you are found for the searches your customers actually type, not only for your own name.

sections.title: How much does a website cost in Geel?
paragraphs: A website from me usually costs {websiteRange}, depending on the number of pages and what the site needs to do. That is a fixed price, in writing before I start. As a small business I'm VAT-exempt (art. 56bis WBTW), so nothing is added. A site is usually ready in {websiteWeeksMin} to {websiteWeeksMax} weeks.
If you want to know for your own project, the cost estimate on this site gives you a price range with a breakdown in a few questions, without leaving an email address.

sections.title: What a local business needs online
paragraphs: An address, phone number and opening hours that are the same everywhere: on your site, in Google Maps and in the directories you're listed in. If they differ, Google can't tell which one is right.
A site that loads quickly on a phone, even with a weak signal. Someone searching from the car or a building site won't wait ten seconds.
Real photos of your business and your work instead of stock images, and text that says what you do in the words your customers use.

cases.note: Carrosserie Kris in Grobbendonk, in the Kempen: I have built and run their website since 2021. It is one of the business's main channels, with enquiries coming in straight through the site.
Banden Leusch, also in Grobbendonk: a full-service garage and tyre centre. In 2026 I replaced their old website with a new one, which I have hosted and maintained since.

kust.metaTitle: Website development in Blankenberge and Bruges
kust.metaDescription: A fast website for your business on the Belgian coast, built for tourists on their phones. Web developer in Blankenberge and Bruges, at a fixed price.
kust.title: Having a website built on the coast, from Blankenberge to Bruges
intro: A lot on the coast depends on the season. Tourists search on their phones for somewhere to eat, stay or rent something, often only once they have arrived. A site that loads slowly or reads badly on a small screen costs you customers right there.

I build websites for businesses in Blankenberge, Bruges and the surrounding area that are ready for that: fast, clear on a small screen, and with your opening hours, menu or rates where visitors expect them. A French or German version for visitors from across the border can be added too.
I work independently, without middlemen. You know the price before I start, and after launch I'm still around for the changes a new season brings.

sections.title: For businesses in Blankenberge, Bruges and the area around them
paragraphs: I work from Blankenberge for businesses along this stretch of coast and just inland: Blankenberge, Zeebrugge, Wenduine, De Haan, Knokke-Heist and Bruges. Restaurants, accommodation, rentals and shops that depend on visitors, but also tradespeople and service businesses that work all year round.

sections.title: What a coastal business needs online
paragraphs: Opening hours that change with the season, and that match on your site and in Google Maps. A closed door where Google says 'open' costs you more than one customer.
A menu, price list or rates as plain text on the page, not as a PDF or a photo. That reads easily on a phone, and search engines can read it.

A clear button to book, call or get directions, at the top of the screen. If many of your visitors speak French or German, a version in their language: you supply the translations, I build the language versions.

sections.title: How much does a website cost on the coast?
paragraphs: Usually {websiteRange}, as a fixed price agreed before I start. An extra language or a booking module comes as a separate item, and the quote shows what each item costs. No VAT is added, because I'm VAT-exempt as a small business (art. 56bis WBTW).
If you are planning a new site for the season, start in time: most sites are ready in {websiteWeeksMin} to {websiteWeeksMax} weeks, and you want yours online before the first busy weekends.

pricingGuide.tableTitle: What a website or web application costs, by type of project
pricingGuide.tableIntro: These are the price ranges the cost estimate above works with. Where your project falls within a range depends on the points below; the estimate works it out for you.

drivers.title: The number of pages or screens
drivers.body: Every page has to be designed, built and tested. A five-page site costs less than a twenty-page one; for a web application the same goes for screens.

drivers.title: The design
drivers.body: A simple, clean design based on your logo and colours, a custom design, or a distinctive design with more elements of its own. The more custom, the more hours.

drivers.title: The text
drivers.body: If you supply finished text, it costs nothing extra. If you want it edited or written from scratch, that is added per page.

drivers.title: What the site needs to do
drivers.body: A contact form, blog, photo gallery, online booking, a web shop or customer accounts: each feature has its own price, and you choose what goes in.

drivers.title: Languages
drivers.body: A second language needs a one-off setup and some work per page. You supply the translations themselves.

drivers.title: New, rebuild or extension
drivers.body: A new site starts from scratch. For a rebuild I move the content from your old site; for an existing application I read the code before I change anything. Each is listed separately in the estimate.

sections.title: A fixed price, not hourly billing
paragraphs: You get a price in writing before I start, and it does not change once we agree. If you want to add something along the way, you hear what it costs before I build it. So you never get an invoice for hours you did not see coming.

sections.title: Who owns what I build?
paragraphs: You do. The code and the domain are yours, and the domain is registered in your name. If you later want to continue with another developer or hosting company, you take everything with you, at no extra cost and without buying anything back.

sections.title: Comparing quotes
paragraphs: If you are comparing several quotes, ask every provider the same questions:
list: Is the price fixed, or an estimate based on hours?
Who owns the code and the domain after handover?
Who actually builds the site: the person you talk to, or someone else?
Is it an original design, or a template or page builder with your logo on it?
How fast does the site load on a phone, and can you see an example that is already live?
